lines.japanese:
ボンジョワール！
　なんだかあっさりとデッドエンドを迎えてしまったいけない遠野くんの為のこのコーナー、
“おしえて！
知得留先生”の時間がやってきちゃいました。
　これから長いお付き合いになりますから、今後ともどうぞよろしくお願いします。
　ちなみに、生徒は全国うん千人の遠野くんと、
「にゃによー、この扱いのさはー」
　月姫における正ヒロイン、アルクェイドさんです。
　それでは一時間目の授業を始めますね！
lines.label: s511
lines.maoEnglish:
Bonjour!
This little feature is for that naughty Tohno, who somehow stumbled into a dead end with ridiculous ease,
and now it’s time for “Teach Me, Ciel!” Class is in session!
We’ll be together for quite some time, so I hope you’ll keep joining us.
Our students, incidentally, are the several thousand Tohnos scattered across the nation, and—
“Whyyy do I get treated so much worse?”
—Arcueid, the principal heroine of TSUKIHIME.
Now, let lesson one begin!

lines.japanese:
もー、だめですね遠野くんは。
　いくらなんでもこんな終わり方はあんまりでしょう？
　あんなエタイの知れない吸血鬼と仲良くなりたくない、という気持ちは解りますが、ここはぐっとガマンの子です。
　人間生き残るためには忍耐も必要だし、長いものには巻かれろ、Ｎｏと言えない日本人の本領を発揮しちゃってください。
　あ、あと問答無用でドッグフードになってしまった遠野くんは、もっと前から再提出です。
　路地裏での返答は自由ですが、逃げ出すのだけはよろしくないのでは、と。
lines.label: s511
lines.maoEnglish:
Honestly, Tohno, you’re hopeless.
Ending things this way was a little much, don’t you think?
I understand not wanting to make friends with a thoroughly suspicious vampire, but this is where you grit your teeth and bear it.
Survival takes patience; bow to the inevitable, bend with the wind, and show us the true mettle of a Japanese man who can’t say no.
Oh, and if Tohno was summarily turned into dog food, he’ll need to redo his work from even farther back.
Answer however you like in the alley, but running away is perhaps not the wisest response.

　二時間目は野生の動物に関してレクチャーします。

Until next time, everyone—goodbyyyye!

　慎重なのはいいと思いますが、今回は裏目に出ましたね。
　基本的に遠野くんはヒーローなんですから、多少の無茶は許されます。
　許されますが、さすがに鮫なんていう不条理な動物には対処しきれませんでした。
　このさいアルクェイドなんてうっちゃっておいて、

Question rejected.

Caution is generally admirable, but this time it worked against you.
As the hero, you are allowed a certain amount of recklessness.
Unfortunately, even a hero was no match for an animal as unreasonable as a shark.
At this point, forget about Arcueid and—

…………はあ。
　遠野くん、一体なにをしていたんですか。
　まさか幻の三時間目と言われた“がくがく動物ランドそのニ”の講習にくるなんて思ってもいませんでした。

lines.label: s513

Haaah.
Tohno, what on earth were you doing?
I never dreamed you would attend the supposedly mythical third lesson, Trembling Animal Kingdom, Part Two.
――――Now then, Tohno.
Regrettably, you must resubmit your work.
You drifted aimlessly through your days and failed to pay enough attention to Arcueid, Ciel, or Akiha.

lines.japanese:
実を言うとですね、ここはシエルさんルートの本命です。
　だっていうのに死んでしまったのは、遠野くんはある人からお守りを貰ってないからなんです。
　これにこりたら学校の先輩にかまうこと！
　一つ、放課後は茶道室。
　一つ、過ちを犯してしまったら素直に認める。
　以上のポイントを押さえておけば試験は安心です。
　それでは三時間目の授業はここまで。
　今度はこっちにこないよう、頑張ってください。
lines.label: s513
lines.maoEnglish:
To tell the truth, this is a crucial point on Ciel’s route.
You died because you never received a protective charm from a certain person.
Let that teach you to spend time with your upperclassman at school!
First: visit the tea-ceremony room after school.
Second: when you make a mistake, admit it honestly.
Remember those points and you’ll have nothing to fear from the exam.
That concludes lesson three.
Do your best not to visit us again.

Please try hard so you won't end up here again next time.

lines.japanese:
―――気がつくと朝になっていた。
　雨は止んだらしく、ざあ、という雨だれの音は聞こえない。
　外は曇っているようで、窓ごしの陽射しはそう明るくはなかった。
「は――――あ」
　長くため息をついて、ベッドから起きあがる。
　……昨夜は深く眠れなかった。
　うつらうつらと眠って、そのたびにあの光景が脳裏に蘇ってすぐに目を覚ましてしまう、といった繰り返しのためだ。
lines.label: s69
lines.maoEnglish:
―――When I came to, it was morning.
The rain seemed to have stopped; its steady drumming was gone.
The sky outside remained overcast, and the sunlight through the window was dim.
“Haaah…”
With a long sigh, I sat up in bed.
I had slept poorly.
Each time I began to drift off, that scene returned to me, and I woke again at once.

lines.mirrorMoon:
---When I come to, it's morning.
Maybe the rain stopped; I can't hear it anymore.
It seems clouded outside, and the sunlight through the window is dim.
"Ha----ah."
Taking a deep breath, I get out of bed.
…… I didn't sleep well last night.
Over and over, as I was about to fall asleep, that scene would replay in my mind and keep me awake.

「……真っ赤な床とバラバラの手足、か……」
　理性や記憶はこういう時に不便だと思う。
　忘れたいコトばかり、逆に思い出させようとするんだから。
lines.label: s69
lines.maoEnglish:
“A floor soaked red, and arms and legs in pieces.”
Reason and memory were badly designed for moments like this.
They insisted on preserving the very things I most wanted to forget.

Reason and memory are liabilities at times like these.
They force me to remember things I only want to forget.

　早く、一刻も早く忘れてしまえ。
　コンコン。
　扉がノックされる。
　時計は朝の六時すぎ。
　……こんな早くから誰だろう、一体？
lines.label: s69
lines.maoEnglish:
“It was only a dream—how long am I going to let it torment me?”
Yes, only a dream.
I needed to forget it, and quickly.
Knock, knock.
Someone knocked at the door.
The clock showed a little after six.
Who could possibly be here this early?

“…”
Hisui falls silent.
Looking closer, I notice my school uniform in her hands.
“Oh, I see. You brought me something to change into.”
“Yes. I am sorry. You have seen me in such an unseemly state.”
“?”
Hisui closes her mouth again.
I have no idea what part of her behavior she considers unseemly.

---One more thing, Nii-san…"
She straightens her posture and looks right at me.
lines.mirror_moon:
"…… Yes, you may be right.
But it is what Father wanted, so I spend half the week here."
"Hmm… but the old man isn't here anymore, so you don't have to force yourself, right?

With things like what happened yesterday, I will still be attending school from the mansion for now.

lines.japanese:
「……えっと……なに？」
「浅上女学院の宿舎は寮ではなく寄宿舎ですから、次からは間違わないでください」
　……なんか、秋葉の言葉には棘がある。
　いや、棘っていったら初日からいっぱいあったけど、今朝のはなんか拗ねているような、そんな感じのとげとげしさだ。
lines.label: s70

“Asagami has a boarding house, not a dormitory, so please remember that next time.”
There was something barbed in Akiha’s voice.
Granted, she had had thorns enough for a whole rosebush since my first day there, but that morning they had a strangely sulky edge.

琥珀さんのことだけど」
「はい？
　琥珀がどうかしましたか？」
「うん、いい人だなって。
さっき玄関で怒られちまったよ。
朝ごはんを抜いたら大きくなれませんよーって」
「ふうん。
たしかに琥珀らしいですね、それは。
兄さんは琥珀の事は気に入りましたか？」

She scolded me in the foyer earlier: ‘You’ll never grow big and strong if you skip breakfast!’”
“I see. That does sound like Kohaku. Do you like her, Brother?”

Food had little to do with my dizzy spells, but this seemed like a good time to nod obediently.

“No, not that. It’s just the four of us living on the estate—you, me, Kohaku, and Hisui—right?
I was wondering which rooms are in use and things like that.”

　ちなみに居間はロビーからすぐ右に曲がったところにある。
秋葉のように言うなら東館一階ロビー手前、というところか。

lines.maoEnglish:

Yours is at the far end of the west wing’s second floor, and mine is at the far end of the east wing.
Hisui’s room is near the stairs on the west wing’s second floor; Kohaku’s is at the front of the west wing’s ground floor.
Father’s room is beside hers; we keep that one open for the time being.”
The sitting room, incidentally, was just to the right of the foyer. In Akiha’s terms, that made it the front room on the ground floor of the east wing.

That forbidden library sounded suspicious in a completely unrelated sort of way, but whatever was going on there surely had nothing to do with me.

「兄さん。

Kohaku called from the dining room.
“Well, that’s my cue; I’m off to eat.”
“Brother. Please stop speaking so crudely.”
Akiha’s gaze sharpened at once.
“There you are, back to your old self. You were much quieter when you were worried about me.”
“I was not worried about you, Brother!”
Akiha turned her face away with a huff.
Smiling at the sight, I went into the dining room.

「いってらっしゃいませ」

「昨夜って、別に何もないよ。
学校で気分が悪くなって、早退して、帰ってくる途中で―――」
―――途中で？
「公園でダウンしただけだから。
まあ、たしかに秋葉の言うとおり軽率ではあったかな。
……うん、これからは気をつけるよ」
lines.label: s73

Hisui saw me out of the house.
“Have a safe journey.”
After offering her usual farewell, Hisui continued to stare at me.
“Master Shiki, what happened yesterday?”
“Last night? Nothing happened; I felt sick at school, left early, and on my way home―――”
―――On my way home?
“I only collapsed in the park, so Akiha was right that I’d been careless. …Yes, I’ll be more careful from now on.”

この交差点を抜けてしばらくすれば正門だ。
　時刻はまだ七時半ごろ。
　今日は余裕をもって登校できそうだ。
　信号器が赤になって、横断歩道の前で立ち止まる。

この歩道の向こうはすでに学校の塀がある。
　通学路だから歩道はガードレールに守られていて、今も我先にと生徒たちが校門へと向かっていた。
　この時間、向かいの歩道にはうちの学校の生徒しかいない。
　しかいない筈だ。
　なのに、車がせわしなく走っていく合間に、白い人影を見た気がした。
lines.label: s73
lines.maoEnglish:
The main gate lay a short way beyond the next intersection.
It was only around seven thirty.
For once, I would arrive with time to spare.
The light turned red, and I stopped at the crossing.
The school wall already ran along the far side.
Guardrails protected the pavement on this busy school route, and students were streaming toward the gate as fast as they could.
At this hour, the opposite pavement held only students from my school.
Or it should have.
Yet between the cars streaming past, I thought I saw a figure in white.

　まわりの生徒たちは向こう側へと歩いていく。

The students around me crossed to the other side.
I alone remained rooted where I stood, staring.

lines.japanese:
彼女はガードレールに腰をかけて、足をぶらぶらとゆらしている。
　まるで何か、誰かを待っているような様子。
　どれくらい待っているのかは見当もつかないけれど、彼女の表情に険しいものはない。
 ───誰を待っているのだろう。
　まるで恋人と待ち合わせをしているふうに、彼女はそわそわして落ち着いていない。

───イヤな、予感がする。

「あ―――――」
　白い女がこっちを見た。
　たぶん、そんなのはただの偶然。
　アレはただ似ているだけの他人で、彼女は別の誰かを待っているに決まってる。
　そうでなければ、この瞬間こそ悪い夢だ。
　だって、彼女はこの手で、完膚なきまでに殺したはずなんだから――――
lines.label: s73
lines.maoEnglish:
She sat on the guardrail, swinging her legs idly.
She looked as though she were waiting for someone.
I had no idea how long she had been there, but there was no anger in her face.
───Who could she be waiting for?
She fidgeted with the restless anticipation of someone waiting to meet her lover.
───Dread crawled through me.
“Ah―――――”
The woman in white looked my way.
It was probably only a coincidence.
She had to be a stranger who merely resembled the dead girl, waiting for someone else.
Otherwise this very moment was the nightmare.
I had killed her with these hands, utterly and beyond all hope of survival――――

けれど、女はこっちを見て笑っていた。
『やっと来たわね』と自分を殺した相手を見付けて、心の底から満足そうに――――
　女は親しげに手をあげて笑みをむけると、ガードレールから腰をあげた。
　さらり、と髪をなびかせてこっちに向かってくる。
「───────来る、な」
　悪い、夢だ。
　信号が赤になる。

「―――――――来るな、よ」
　彼女は気にした風もなく、車が行き交う道路を一直線に横断してくる。
　あと、ほんの数メートルも距離はない。
lines.label: s73
lines.maoEnglish:
But the woman looked at me and smiled.
She had found the person who killed her, and her face shone with heartfelt satisfaction, as though to say, There you are at last――――
The woman raised one hand in a familiar greeting, smiled, and rose from the guardrail.
Her hair streaming lightly, she walked toward me.
“───────Don’t come closer”
This was a nightmare.
The signal turned red.
“―――――――Stay away”
Paying no attention, she walked straight across the road through the moving traffic.
Only a few meters remained between us.

I made some sound I could not understand and fled from the woman in white.
lines.mao_english:

　全力で走った。
　恥も外聞もなく、通り過ぎる人達を弾きとばしながら、アスファルトの上を全力疾走した。
「はっ、はっ、はっ、はっ─────！」
　呼吸が乱れて、心臓がばくばくと悲鳴をあげる。
　それでも走った。
　走らないと気が狂いそうだった。

I ran with everything I had.
With no thought for shame or appearances, I knocked people aside and sprinted flat-out over the asphalt.
“Hah, hah, hah, hah─────!”
My breath broke apart, and my heart screamed against my ribs.
Still I ran.
If I stopped, I felt I would go mad.

The woman in white was walking after me.

　とことこと軽い足取りで逃げる俺を追ってきている。
「はっ、はっ、はっ、はっ─────！」
　顎があがる。
　両腕がだるい。
　足はとっくに千切れそうだ。
　だっていうのに、
　こんなにも全力で走っているのに、どうして歩いているだけの相手をふりきれないんだ──！
lines.label: s73
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hah, hah, haaah──────!”
Ignoring the heart that felt ready to burst, I kept running.
When I looked back, there she was.
She followed my desperate flight with light, unhurried steps.
“Hah, hah, hah, hah─────!”
My head lolled back.
My arms were dead weights.
My legs had felt ready to tear off long ago.
And yet—when I was sprinting with everything I had,
how could I still fail to outrun someone who was only walking?

lines.japanese:
「はっ、はっ、はっ、はっ────」
　息があがる。
　もう何キロ全力で走ったろうか。
　それでも振り返ればあいつが歩いてやってきている。
　自然に、散歩するような足取りでピッタリとくっついてきている。

「………はっ、はっ、はっ、はは、はははは」
　おかしくもないのに笑って、笑いながらまだ走った。
「はは、ははは、あははははははは！」
　笑いが止まらない。
　それでも走って、これ以上走れば死んでしまうって体が訴えているのに、まだ走った。

走る理由は簡単だ。
　だってあいつに追い付かれたら、俺は間違いなく殺される。
　何を根拠に、と自分自身でそんな妄想を笑い飛ばしても、そんなのが気休めだってのはやっぱり自分自身が一番よくわかっていた。
　理由も根拠も証拠もない。
　ただもう真実として、遠野志貴は、あの女に追い付かれたら殺されるって理解している─────
lines.label: s73
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hah, hah, hah, hah────”
I could scarcely breathe.
How many kilometers had I sprinted?
Still, whenever I looked back, she was walking after me.
Her light, casual steps kept her right behind me, as though she were out for a stroll.
“Hah, hah, hah―――haha, hahahaha”
Nothing was funny, but I laughed, and kept running as I laughed.
“Ha, haha―――ahahahahahaha!”
The laughter would not stop.
My body screamed that another step would kill me, yet I continued to run.
The reason was simple.
If she caught me, I would unquestionably be killed.
I could laugh at my own delusion and ask what possible basis it had, but I knew better than anyone that such mockery was cold comfort.
There was no reason, no basis, no proof.
Shiki Tohno simply understood one truth―――if that woman caught him, she would kill him─────

“Ah───”
I crashed gracelessly to the ground.
I had not tripped; my body could not take another step, and I pitched forward.
“Gh───hah, ah”

Kill it and it comes back.
Snuff out its life and it carries on as if nothing happened.
Tear it to pieces and it simply puts itself back together and starts moving again—something that could never be called human.

First, I needed to look at her carefully.
Then I could think through everything else.

lines.japanese:
「あ、おかえりなさいませ、志貴さん」
　なんて、ロビーに入るなり琥珀さんに笑顔で挨拶をされてしまった。
「あ……ああ、ただいま。
あの、琥珀さん？」
「ええ、朝ごはんですね？
　すぐに支度をしますから居間で待っていてください。
秋葉さまも先ほど済ませたばかりですから」
　琥珀さんはパタパタと音をたてて居間の方へ去っていってしまった。

……平和すぎる。
　昨日の女性の死体はまだ発見されていないんだろうか。
「………………」
　とりあえず制服を着替えに自室に戻る事にしよう。
lines.label: s74
lines.maoEnglish:
“Oh, welcome home, Shiki.”
Kohaku greeted me with a smile the instant I entered the lobby.
“Ah… I’m home. Kohaku, is―――” “Breakfast?
I’ll prepare it at once, so please wait in the sitting room. Miss Akiha only just finished hers.”
Kohaku hurried toward the sitting room with quick, pattering footsteps.
It was too peaceful.
Had they still not found the woman’s body from yesterday?
“…”
For the moment, I decided to return to my room and change uniforms.

lines.japanese:
自分の部屋に戻ると翡翠がいた。
「―――おはようございます、志貴さま。
お帰りになられたのですね」
「うん、ついさっき。
……あのさ、翡翠。
悪いんだけど、替えの制服ってある？

すぐにご用意いたします」

lines.label: s74
lines.maoEnglish:
Hisui was there when I entered my room.
“―――Good morning, Master Shiki. You have returned.”
“Yeah. I just got back. Hisui, do I have another uniform? The one I’m wearing got soaked in yesterday’s rain.”
“Certainly. I shall prepare it immediately.”
Hisui bowed and left without a sound.
Once she returned, I changed into the fresh uniform and went to the sitting room.

away.

“――――Ah.”
Right—I was supposed to have left school early yesterday.

「雨にうたれたぐらいで貧血を起こすなんて、兄さん、体の具合が悪いんじゃないですか？
　一度主治医に看てもらうにしても、登下校は車で送ってもらったほうがいいんじゃありません？」
「…………」
　なるほど。
そういった理由で有彦の家に泊まった、という事になっているのか。

「大丈夫、秋葉が気にするような事じゃない。
ちゃんと月に一回は病院に通ってるし、車なんかで送られたらそれこそ体が鈍るだろ。
　秋葉が俺のことでそこまで神経質になることはないよ。
ま、心配してくれるのは嬉しいんだけどさ」
「……そんなこと、ないです。
私、兄さんの心配なんてしてません、から」
　ふい、と微妙に秋葉は視線を逸らした。
lines.label: s74
lines.maoEnglish:
“If being caught in the rain is enough to make you collapse from anemia, perhaps you’re unwell, Brother. You should see your doctor. Perhaps you should even have a car take you to and from
school.”
“…” So that was the story: I had become ill in the rain and stayed at Arihiko’s house.
“I’m fine. I visit the hospital every month, and being driven everywhere would only make me weaker.
You don’t need to be this nervous over me. Though I am glad you care.”
“――That isn’t true. I’m not worried about you, Brother.”
Akiha looked away slightly.

lines.label: s74
lines.maoEnglish:
“Shiki, everything’s ready!”
Kohaku called from the dining room.
“Well, I’m off to eat.”
“Honestly, Brother, please stop speaking so crudely.” Akiha’s gaze sharpened.
“Ah.
There you are. You’re finally back to normal. It doesn’t feel right unless you’re like this, so stop worrying about me and relax.”
“―――You are infuriating! I told you I am not worried about you, Brother!”
Akiha jerks her face away.
Smiling at the sight, I went to the dining room.

“Nothing. I was caught in the rain and had an anemic spell. I’ll be more careful.”
“I am not reproaching you. Master Shiki merely appears to be forcing himself this morning. Please take great care along the way.”

lines.japanese:
翡翠は深々とおじぎをして俺を送り出した。
 ……まいったな。
　できるだけ平静にふるまって、秋葉にも琥珀さんにもボロをださなかったっていうのに、翡翠には通じなかったらしい。
「……もしかして気遣ってくれたのかな、翡翠」
　いつも淡々とした彼女の感情はわかりにくい。
　ともかく、今日が最後の登校になるかもしれないんだ。
　できるだけいつも通りに、悔いの残らないような一日にしよう────。
lines.label: s74
lines.maoEnglish:
Hisui bowed deeply as she saw me out.
So much for that.
I had behaved as calmly as possible and kept both Akiha and Kohaku from noticing anything, yet Hisui had seen through me.
“Was that her way of worrying about me?”
Her emotions were difficult to read beneath that constant composure.
In any case, this might be my last day of school.
I would live it as normally as possible and leave nothing to regret.──────

lines.japanese:
どんなにこっちの心境が複雑でも、朝の様子は変わらない。
　学校に近付くにつれ、学生服姿の生徒たちを多く見かけるようになってくる。
　休日前の土曜日。
　遠野志貴にとって、学校というものはこれで最後になるかもしれないかと思うと、歩いている足が止まりそうになる。
　それでもできるだけ平静に、二年間馴染んだ通学路を歩いていく。
　この交差点を抜けてしばらくすれば校門が見えてくる。
lines.label: s74
lines.maoEnglish:
However tangled my feelings, the morning itself remained unchanged.
As I approached the school, more and more students in uniform appeared.
It was Saturday, the day before a holiday.
The thought that this might be Shiki Tohno’s final day as a student nearly stopped my feet.
Even so, I followed the route I had known for two years, doing my best to remain calm.
Beyond this intersection, the school gate would soon come into view.

Even so, I followed the route I had known for two years, doing my best to remain calm.
Beyond this intersection, the school gate would soon come into view.

lines.maoEnglish:

At that hour, the only people on the far sidewalk should have been students from my school.
They should have been the only ones there.
Yet between the ceaselessly passing cars, I thought I saw a figure in white.

Tear it to pieces and it simply puts itself back together and starts moving again—something that could never be called human.

lines.maoEnglish:
“Hello? Are you listening, you homicidal maniac?”
“Yeah, I’m listening. I’m just taking in how spectacularly unlucky I am. Sorry, but could you be quiet for a moment?”
───Honestly, what rotten luck.
For no reason at all, I had suddenly wanted to kill a woman I’d never met—and then, carried by that impulse, I had done it.
I had suffered, despaired, and finally resolved to find some way of atoning; now, just as I made that decision, I learned the person I had killed was never human in the first place.

“But―――vampires don’t exist.”

“……”
I didn’t.

You probably can’t imagine it, but returning to life takes a considerable amount of strength.

As a result, reviving consumed nearly all my strength—”

I couldn't heal the wounds, so I had no choice but to remake my body parts.
That's why it took so much energy to revive---"

“―――This is bad”
The woman murmured.
The crow watched us without blinking.
“Honestly! You took so long that we’ve been found.”
The woman was looking toward the mouth of the alley.
“Found by what?”
I turned toward the alley entrance.
―――――And then.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"---Oh, man…"
The girl murmurs.
The crow just stares at us.
"Geez, thanks to your slowness, he found us."
The girl looks at the entrance to the alley.
"Found us?
Who?"
I cast my gaze towards the alley entrance.
-----Then.

lines.japanese:
「―――――！」
　びくっ、と思わず体が一歩引いてしまった。
　いつのまにか、路地裏の入り口である細い道に一匹の犬がいた。
　どこか歪つフォルムをした強靭な四肢と、ピン、とはりつめた鉄骨のような首。
　
　人間とは大きくかけはなれた、『獲物を狩る』ことだけを追求したそのフォルム。
lines.label: s75
lines.maoEnglish:
“―――――!”
I flinched back a step.
At some point, a dog had appeared in the narrow passage leading into the alley.
Its powerful limbs were subtly misshapen, its neck taut as an iron beam.
Its form was wholly unlike a human body, honed for one purpose alone: hunting prey.
lines.mao_english:
“―――――!”
I flinched back a step.
At some point, a dog had appeared in the narrow passage leading into the alley.
Its powerful limbs were subtly misshapen, its neck taut as an iron beam.
Its form was wholly unlike a human body, honed for one purpose alone: hunting prey.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"-----!"
I take a step back in shock.
Before I knew it, a dog had appeared in the narrow path running into the alley.
It has four tough legs and a tense neck like steel frame.
That form, far removed from that of a human, is one made solely for hunting.

lines.japanese:
……そこに、言葉による威嚇など必要ない。
　たいていの人間は、この種の『狩猟』動物を見ただけで緊張してしまう。
　その、同じ生物として、絶望的なまでに優れた運動能力への畏敬として。
lines.label: s75
lines.maoEnglish:
It needed no verbal threat.
Most people tense up at the mere sight of a predator like that.
It is an instinctive awe at the hopeless superiority of another creature’s physical ability.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
…… It doesn't need to resort to verbal intimidation.
Most humans would become nervous just by looking at that kind of "hunting" beast.
As a fellow life form, it inspires awe by its dishearteningly superior athletic ability.

lines.japanese:
「……黒い、犬……？」
―――びくん、と体が震える。
　……こっちを見ているあの黒犬は野犬と言い捨てられる大きさじゃない。
　シェパードとかドーベルマンほどの大きさをした黒犬は、ただそこにいるだけでこちらを威圧しているようだった。
lines.label: s75
lines.maoEnglish:
“A black dog?”
―――My body convulsed with a shudder.
The black dog staring at us was far too large to dismiss as a stray.
As big as a shepherd or Doberman, it seemed to menace us merely by standing there.

lines.mirrorMoon:

As big as a German Shepherd or a Doberman, it just stands there, menacing us.

「…………」
　彼女は何も言わず、つまらなそうな目をして黒犬を見つめている。
lines.label: s75
lines.maoEnglish:
“……”
The woman said nothing, watching the black dog with a look of utter boredom.
lines.mao_english:
“……”
The woman said nothing, watching the black dog with a look of utter boredom.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"………"
The girl says nothing, but looks at the dog with disinterested eyes.
lines.mirror_moon:
"………"
The girl says nothing, but looks at the dog with disinterested eyes.

lines.japanese:
と。
　唐突に、黒犬は跳んだ。
　いや、走ってきた。
ただそのスピードが速すぎて、跳んだとしか認識できない。
「――――――え？」
　何もできない。
　黒い犬は、その予備動作さえ感じさせないまま俺の喉元へと飛びついてくる。

見えているのに。
　黒い肢体がやってくるのが見えているのに、自分は避ける事も、避けようという考えもうかばなかった。

ドン、という衝撃が体に走る。
「ぐっ―――――！」
　いきなり横殴りに弾き飛ばされた。
　黒犬に食いつかれた事による衝撃じゃない。
　俺の体は、黒い犬に首を噛み砕かれる前に、いきなり女に弾き飛ばされたらしい。
　その、まるでボールでも投げるような無造作な動作で、女は俺を片手で壁際まですっとばした。
lines.label: s75
lines.maoEnglish:
And then.
Without warning, the black dog leaped.
No—it ran. It was simply so fast that I could perceive it only as a leap.
“――――――What?”
I could do nothing.
Without even seeming to prepare itself, the black dog sprang at my throat.
I could see it.
I could see that black body rushing toward me, yet neither the act nor even the thought of dodging occurred to me.
A heavy impact jolted my body.
“Guh―――――!”
Something knocked me violently sideways.
It wasn’t the impact of the dog’s jaws.
Before the beast could crush my throat, the woman had apparently swatted me out of its path.
With one careless motion, as though tossing a ball, she flung me one-handed all the way to the wall.

“Guh―――――!”

lines.mirrorMoon:
Then…
Suddenly, the black dog jumps.
No, it's running, but with a speed that makes it seem like it's jumping.
"------Eh?"
I can't do anything.
The black dog jumps straight for my throat.

I can see it.
I can see its black body moving towards me, but I don't even have time to think about dodging it.

Thud!
I feel a shock on my body.
"Guh-----!"
I was hit hard from the side.
It's not the black dog.
It seems the girl pushed me before it could crush my throat.
With an easy movement, like someone throwing a ball, she hurls me into the wall using just one hand.

「っ―――――！」
　ダン、と派手な音をたてて、俺は尻餅をついてしまっている。
「こ……のぉ！
　おまえ、いきなり何するんだ！」
「いいから前！」
　女が叫ぶ。
　見れば―――俺という標的を失った黒犬は、そのまま壁まで跳躍していた。
　ぴたり、と黒犬はトカゲのように壁に張り付いて、また跳んだ。
　タン、と壁からこちらに向かって反射してくる。
　黒犬の軌跡は、さながら黒い稲妻のようだった。
lines.label: s75
lines.maoEnglish:
“―――――!”
I hit the ground with a tremendous bang and landed hard on my backside.
“You… you—! What the hell was that for?”
“Look in front of you!”
The woman shouted.
When I looked―――the black dog, deprived of its target, had carried its leap all the way to the wall.
It clung there like a lizard, then sprang again and rebounded toward me with a tap.
Its path was a bolt of black lightning.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"-----!"
With a terrific "wham!", I fall on my rear.
"Why… you!
What in the world are you doing!?"
"Never mind that, keep your eyes in front!"

I look---Having lost sight of me, its target, the black dog bounds towards the wall.
Sticking to the wall like a lizard, it jumps again.
It bounces from the wall towards me.
The dog's path is like black lightning.

「くっ………！」

The black dog opened a mouth slick with fangs and saliva and lunged for my throat once more――――
“Urgh…!”

　喉に、黒犬の牙が食い込む。
　が、その瞬間。
　きゃん、と鳴き声をあげて、黒犬の牙は俺の喉元から離れていった。

I felt the black dog’s fangs sink into my throat.
But at that instant.
With a yelp, its fangs pulled away from my throat.

It was smashed violently into the concrete.

“I’m an exception. Oh—looks like I’m at my limit. Good night, Shiki. Wake me when the sun goes down.”
“H-hey.”
“—”
Like a machine whose battery had died, Arcueid fell asleep without warning.

lines.label: s80
lines.maoEnglish:
“Haaah.”
How could anyone be this defenseless?
“You know, I could just run away.”
She had practically dragged me here, and right now escaping would be effortless.
Not that the old impulse was stirring in me anymore.
“After all—I’ve already killed you once.”
So how could this woman simply fall asleep in front of me?
“…”
I studied Arcueid’s sleeping face.
The rise and fall of her full breasts showed that she was breathing, yet the rest of her body never stirred.
The air around her alone seemed to have stopped,
a stillness so absolute that merely looking at her threatened to stop me too.
―――What a peaceful sleep.
She lay utterly defenseless, as though she trusted me completely even though we had only just met.

lines.maoEnglish:
“Me? I’m hunting a vampire. Killing vampires is my role.”
“You have mentioned that. But Arcueid—you’re a vampire too, aren’t you?”
“What? You still don’t believe me, Shiki?”
“Unfortunately, I believe you more than enough, so don’t worry.

“Oh? You don’t like your own kind killing one another?”
Like or dislike had nothing to do with it. I wasn’t fond of killing in the first place. Still, a vampire killing a vampire simply felt wrong.

lines.maoEnglish:
“We use the word vampire broadly, but there are two major kinds: those born as vampires, and those who became vampires.
The former are called True Ancestors; the latter are Dead Apostles.

Our enemy is a vampire classified as a Dead Apostle.”

Dead Apostles—the vampiric species that were not born that way—possess only an imperfect immortality.
They no longer age, so old age cannot kill them. But unless they constantly replenish the energy that sustains that immortality, they will disappear. No living thing can function without nourishment, can it? It is no different for them.
Vampires simply have no natural lifespan as long as they continue feeding.”

It's just that vampires don't die from age as long as they take in the nutrients."

lines.maoEnglish:
“Dead Apostles drink blood because their survival depends on it.
They began as human beings, and the human body was never meant to be immortal.
From the moment they become a different kind of vessel—a vampiric species—the genes composing their bodies decay at a ferocious rate.
They compensate by drinking another person’s blood, absorbing its genetic information, and using it to stabilize their own bodies. For vampires, drinking blood is not a meal but the bare minimum needed to continue existing.”

lines.mirrorMoon:
"The Dead Apostles suck blood because they need it to stay alive.
Immortality is a strain on their originally-human bodies.
The genes that compose their bodies are different… when they become vampires, they begin to degenerate at an incredible rate.
To make up for that, they must drain the blood of others in order to absorb genetic information and stabilize their own bodies.
To a vampire, drinking blood is not like eating, but it's the minimum requirement for them to continue to exist."

“Next.
Paralyzing someone with a look is one form of Mystic Eyes. The eyes, along with speech, are among the principal channels for magecraft, so many vampiric species possess Mystic Eyes.
Most of ours are the entrancing kind.
Rather than captivating anyone we look at, they captivate whoever looks into our eyes. A powerful vampire can drive its will straight through its eyes into another person’s brain and seize complete control of their thoughts, though a Dead Apostle’s Mystic Eyes usually aren’t that strong.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"So, moving on.
The ability to bind someone with just a look is a type of Mystic Eyes.
Eyes and words are both common types of magic circuits, so there are many vampires who have Mystic Eyes.
We usually possess the Mystic Eyes of Enchantment.
We don't enchant people by looking at them, rather, we enchant those who look into our eyes.
A powerful vampire using Mystic Eyes can impose his own will into the brain of another and completely dominate their thoughts, but the Mystic Eyes of a Dead Apostle doesn't have that much power."

lines.label: s81
lines.maoEnglish:
Transforming into a wolf—or some other animal—is a by-product of repairing a damaged body with familiars.
The longer a vampire has lived, the less ordinary living creatures can provide what its damaged body needs for repairs.
Humans are physically weak as animals, so it is more efficient to absorb wild beasts that are naturally stronger than we are.
Vampires who have rebuilt their bodies with beasts can restore those beasts to their original forms when needed and command them as familiars.”

Vampires who have rebuilt their bodies with beasts can restore those beasts to their original forms when needed and command them as familiars.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
Wolves--and other animal transformations--are a byproduct of a vampire's repairing its damaged body from its familiars.
For a vampire living a long time, stabilizing their bodies with normal lives is not sufficient.
Humans are not fundamentally powerful animals, so it's more effective to repair one's body by absorbing beasts, as they surpass the human species in this respect.
Vampires who repair their own bodies with beasts can return those beasts to their previous forms and use them as familiars when they need to."

No, not even those could have ‘killed’ me that completely.

Arcueid glared at me like an indignant cat. But no matter how she looked at me, I had nothing to hide—or rather, I did.

They're difficult to see in the daytime due to the strong sunlight, but under the faint moonlight, I can even see the glow coming from the 'lines'.
Amidst them,
the lines on Arcueid's body are very thin.
If I don't concentrate, I lose sight of them of them altogether.

lines.japanese:
「あ―――」
「……志貴にやられてなければきっと完全に視えないでしょうけど、今はたぶん視えてると思う。
　わたしね、夜は『死期』がないんだけど、昼間は多少できてしまうのよ。
　志貴がわたしを殺せたのは昼間だったからだけど、その後の蘇生で力を失ってしまっているから、今は夜でも『死期』ができてしまってる。
　―――ようするに不老不死でなくなったわけだけど、志貴、わたしの体の線が切れる？」
lines.label: s81
lines.maoEnglish:
“Ah—”
“If you hadn’t done this to me, you probably wouldn’t be able to see them at all, but I think you can now.
At night I normally have no appointed death, though a faint one appears during the day.
That is why you could kill me then, but reviving afterward cost me so much power that now, even at night, I have an appointed death.
―――In other words, I’m no longer immortal, so tell me, Shiki: can you cut the lines on my body?”
lines.mao_english:
“Ah—”
“If you hadn’t done this to me, you probably wouldn’t be able to see them at all, but I think you can now.
At night I normally have no appointed death, though a faint one appears during the day.
That is why you could kill me then, but reviving afterward cost me so much power that now, even at night, I have an appointed death.
―――In other words, I’m no longer immortal, so tell me, Shiki: can you cut the lines on my body?”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Ah---"
"…… If I hadn't been killed by you, I don't think you'd be able to see any at all, but right now you can probably see them.
You see, although I have no 'times of death' during the night, some do appear during the day.
You could kill me because it was during daytime, but you can see my 'time of death' during nighttime now since I've used up a lot of energy to regenerate myself.
---In other words, I've lost my immortality.
So, can you cut the lines on my body, Shiki?"

「――――」
　……どうだろう。
　たしかに線があるんだから切れるとは思うけど、あの時のように鮮やかに、一秒もかけずに切断するのは出来そうに無い。
lines.label: s81
lines.maoEnglish:
“……”
I wondered.
There were lines, so I thought I could cut them; but I doubted I could slice her apart as cleanly as I had then, in less than a second.

lines.mirrorMoon:

…… Let's see.
I think I probably could, since the lines are there, but I don't think I could do it so briskly and without hesitation like that time before.

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: Looking at Arcueid's faint lines, Shiki says he could not dismember her as cleanly and in under one second as he did before. mirror moon replaces the explicit time limit with 'without hesitation,' changing a judgment about motor performance into a new claim about psychological reluctance.
mirrorMoonErrors.title: Shiki's lost speed and precision become moral hesitation

lines.japanese:
「……やりにくいと思う。
線が視えたり視えなかったりするから、アルクェイドが眠ってでもいないかぎり、できない」
「でしょう？
　それが貴方の最大の欠点ね。
どんなに『死』が見えていようとも、その『線』を引くのは志貴自身の腕じゃないといけない。
　いくらわたしが弱ってるからって、志貴に掴まるほど運動能力は低下してないもの」
lines.label: s81
lines.maoEnglish:
“It would be hard. The lines keep fading in and out. I couldn’t do it unless you were asleep or something.”
“Exactly. That is your greatest weakness. However clearly you see ‘death,’ it still takes your own hand to trace the line.
I may be weakened, but not so badly that you could ever catch me.”

"You can't, right?

……そっか。
　言われてみれば、俺はすばしっこく動く動物を捕まえることが出来ない。

　つまり、こんな『線』が見えていても動くモノを殺す事は出来ないってコトか。

lines.maoEnglish:
Of course…
I can’t catch a quick-moving animal.
If I can’t catch it, I can’t touch its body.
So even with these lines in sight, I can’t kill anything that can move.

　『線』を見ていると頭痛がおこるのは子供のころから同じだ。
　メガネをかけて視界をもとに戻す。
lines.label: s81
lines.maoEnglish:
“Ow—”
Pain lanced through my head.
Seeing the lines had given me headaches since I was a child.
I put my glasses back on, returning the world to normal.

lines.japanese:
「……………」
　アルクェイドはじーっ、とこちらの様子を見つめている。
「……なんだよ。
まだ何かあるのか」
「ううん、そうじゃなくて。
志貴はそのメガネをかけていれば『線』が見えないの？」
「まあ、そうだけど。
昔、俺の目がこうなったときに出会ったひとがくれたんだ。
今じゃレンズだけしか使ってないけど、これのおかげでなんとか普通に生活が送れてるんだよ」
lines.label: s81
lines.maoEnglish:
“……”
Arcueid studied me intently.
“What? Is there still something else?”
“No, that’s not it. Shiki, do those glasses keep you from seeing the lines?”
“More or less. Someone I met when my eyes first became like this gave them to me. I only use the lenses from the original pair now, but thanks to them I can live a reasonably normal life.”

“I see. Good—one less adversary to worry about. Though if the Blue were involved, retreat would probably be the wisest choice.”
Arcueid fell gravely silent.

　だいたいな、このメガネがないと正気じゃいられないって言ったのはおまえだろ。
それとも俺にそうなれって言いたいのかよ、おまえは」

I rolled across the bed, putting distance between us.
“Oh, you ran away!”
“Of course I did. Listen, I’m not giving you these glasses. If you happened to break them, there’s no replacement.
Besides, you’re the one who said I couldn’t stay sane without them. Or are you saying you want me to lose my mind?”

Arcueid made an ostentatious show of looking away.

I don’t know what you’re plotting, but without these glasses I won’t be in any condition to help you. If I had to see those lines every hour of the day, the headaches would split my skull before I had time to go mad.”

　けど、だからって自分にできない事を強制されるのは何か違うと思う。
　……けど、アルクェイドは眠っている。
　仮にも一度、彼女を殺害してしまった遠野志貴を信用しきって、安らかに眠っている。
lines.label: s84
lines.maoEnglish:
“――――――”
I still wanted to live in the sane, ordinary world.
Of course I felt responsible for killing Arcueid.
But that didn’t make it right to force me into something beyond my power.
And yet Arcueid was asleep—resting peacefully because she trusted Shiki Tohno completely,
though he had already murdered her once.

lines.mirrorMoon:

…… But again, Arcueid is asleep.

lines.maoEnglish:

Even so—I couldn’t do this.
I started walking quietly.
Turning my back on Arcueid as she slept in complete trust, I left the hotel room.

Arcueid had rented every room on the eleventh and highest floor, so the two of us were the only people up here.
“—”

　少し頭を冷やしたくて、公園に向かう事にした。

I took the train from the hotel back to my own city.
It was shortly past noon.
School would soon be ending, so I could probably return to the mansion without raising questions.
“…”
But I felt no desire to go home.
Wanting to clear my head, I went to the park instead.

A sigh escaped me.
I sat on a bench and stared blankly at the sky.
It was still overcast—the perfect image of my mind.

I had killed her once, and she had said she forgave me.
She had forgiven me—so what was I doing here?

昨日の夜。
　アルクェイドを殺してしまったあと、どんな方法でも、自分なりの償いをしようって誓ったのに。

「……………くっ」

Last night, after killing Arcueid, I had sworn to atone in whatever way I could.
Had that oath meant so little that I would abandon it the instant my own life was at risk?
“…Damn…”
But I valued my life.
As long as I was alive, I could never ignore that fact,
and a moment’s emotion could not make me forget it so easily.

Perhaps the impact had woken the guests, who had gone to complain to the hotel.

The lights went out.
At the same instant—
Countless blows began hammering against the door.

The stench of death and blood.
---I never want to experience something like that again.
If I were to remain with Arcueid, there'd be no question that I would be subjected to that scene again.
If I don't want that, I'll have to go back to the mansion.

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: 君が正しいと思う大人になればいい tells Shiki to become the kind of adult he himself believes right. 'Become an adult and do what you think is right' turns an identity-forming ideal into a generic conduct rule, materially weakening Sensei's ethical instruction even though both versions mention right action.

俺は、自分でもどうかしていると思うけど、あいつの信用を裏切れない。
　たとえアルクェイドが人間じゃないっていっても、遠野志貴を信用してくれたんだ。
　決して許されない俺の罪を、笑顔で許すと言ってくれたんだ。
　なら――――自分の命ぐらい、こっちも笑って差し出すぐらいしなくちゃ恥ずかしい。

lines.maoEnglish:
I might have been out of my mind, but I couldn’t betray her trust.
Human or not, Arcueid had placed her faith in Shiki Tohno.
She had smiled and said she would forgive a crime no one should ever forgive.
If she could do that, I would be ashamed if I couldn’t at least offer up my own life with a smile.

lines.maoEnglish:
“People use the word vampire broadly, but we fall into two main kinds.
Those born as vampires, and those who became vampires.
The former are called True Ancestors; the latter, Dead Apostles.
The creatures humans usually call vampires are Dead Apostles. They drink human blood, turn their victims into thralls, weaken in sunlight, and succumb to baptismal rites.
Our enemy is a vampire classified as a Dead Apostle.”

Our enemy is a vampire classified as a Dead Apostle.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Although we're typically called simply 'vampires', we're divided into two main categories.
Those who were vampires from the start, and those who become vampires.
The former are called True Ancestors, and the latter are called the Dead Apostles.
The ones you call vampires are the Dead Apostles.
They drain the blood of humans and turn them into their slaves.
They're weak against sunlight, and you can vanquish them with a baptism ritual.
Our enemy is one of these Dead Apostles."

　どっちにしたって、吸血鬼となったモノたちは不完全ながらも不老不死の肉体を手に入れるわ」
「…………」
　初めから吸血鬼だったものと、人間から吸血鬼になったものとがいる、ということか。
　……なんだろう。
　この話にはなにかひどい矛盾というか、構造的に大きな欠落があるような気がする。

“Dead Apostles were originally human. Some achieved agelessness at the end of their magecraft; others became thralls after a True Ancestor drank their blood.
Either way, those who become vampires gain bodies that are ageless and immortal, if imperfectly so.”
“…”
So there were creatures born as vampires and humans who became vampires.
What was it?
Something about this explanation felt terribly contradictory, as though its very structure were missing a major piece.

"Dead Apostles were once humans.
They've attained immortality through magic, or had their blood sucked by one of the True Ancestors.
Either way, the ones that become vampires become immortal, even though it's imperfect immortality."
"……"
Those who were vampires from the beginning, and humans who became vampires.
…… What is this?
I get the feeling that there's some kind of huge contradiction to all of this.
It feels like some important fundamental is missing somewhere in this theory.

lines.maoEnglish:
Dead Apostles—the vampiric species that were not born that way—possess only an imperfect immortality.
They no longer age, so old age cannot kill them. But unless they constantly replenish the energy that sustains that immortality, they will disappear. No living thing can function without nourishment, can it? It is no different for them.
Vampires simply have no natural lifespan as long as they continue feeding.”

It's the same thing.
It's just that vampires don't die from age as long as they take in the nutrients."

lines.maoEnglish:
“Dead Apostles drink blood because their survival depends on it.
They began as human beings, and the human body was never meant to be immortal.
From the moment they become a different kind of vessel—a vampiric species—the genes composing their bodies decay at a ferocious rate.
They compensate by drinking another person’s blood, absorbing its genetic information, and using it to stabilize their own bodies. For vampires, drinking blood is not a meal but the bare minimum needed to continue existing.”

They compensate by drinking another person’s blood, absorbing its genetic information, and using it to stabilize their own bodies. For vampires, drinking blood is not a meal but the bare minimum needed to continue existing.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"The Dead Apostles suck blood because they need it to stay alive.
Immortality is a strain on their originally-human bodies.
The genes that compose their bodies are different… when they become vampires, they begin to degenerate at an incredible rate.
To make up for that, they must drain the blood of others in order to absorb genetic information and stabilize their own bodies.
To a vampire, drinking blood is not like eating, but it's the minimum requirement for them to continue to exist."

lines.maoEnglish:
Transforming into a wolf—or some other animal—is a by-product of repairing a damaged body with familiars.
The longer a vampire has lived, the less ordinary living creatures can provide what its damaged body needs for repairs.
Humans are physically weak as animals, so it is more efficient to absorb wild beasts that are naturally stronger than we are.
Vampires who have rebuilt their bodies with beasts can restore those beasts to their original forms when needed and command them as familiars.”

“A catalyst steeped in history and human thought! This country has sacred regalia too, doesn’t it? Usually they are Conceptual Weapons for use against nature—staves, swords, jewels, or masks—but Shiki, are you certain you’re not involved with that world?”

Cause and effect. You’ve heard of causality, haven’t you?

　昼間は強い陽射しのおかげで視えにくいけれど、微弱な月の明かりの下では、『線』は光ってさえ視えてしまう。
　その中で。
　アルクェイドの体にある『線』は、ひどくか細く、意識を集中しなくては視えないぐらいだった。
lines.label: s87
lines.maoEnglish:
A white moon hung beyond the window.
Strong sunlight made the lines harder to see by day, but beneath the feeble glow of the moon, they seemed almost to shine.
Among them…
the lines on Arcueid’s body were so terribly faint that I had to concentrate to see them at all.

lines.mirrorMoon:
Outside the window, the moon is white.
They're difficult to see in the daytime due to the strong sunlight, but under the faint moonlight, I can even see the glow coming from the 'lines'.
Amidst them--
The lines on Arcueid's body are very thin.
If I don't concentrate, I lose sight of them of them altogether.

lines.japanese:
「あ―――」
「……志貴にやられてなければきっと完全に視えないでしょうけど、今はたぶん視えてると思う。
　わたしね、夜は『死期』がないんだけど、昼間は多少できてしまうのよ。
　志貴がわたしを殺せたのは昼間だったからだけど、その後の蘇生で力を失ってしまっているから、今は夜でも『死期』ができてしまってる。
　―――ようするに不老不死でなくなったわけだけど、志貴、わたしの体の線が切れる？」
lines.label: s87
lines.maoEnglish:
“Ah—”
“If you hadn’t done this to me, you probably wouldn’t be able to see them at all, but I think you can now.
At night I normally have no appointed death, though a faint one appears during the day.
That is why you could kill me then, but reviving afterward cost me so much power that now, even at night, I have an appointed death.
―――In other words, I’m no longer immortal, so tell me, Shiki: can you cut the lines on my body?”
lines.mao_english:
“Ah—”
“If you hadn’t done this to me, you probably wouldn’t be able to see them at all, but I think you can now.
At night I normally have no appointed death, though a faint one appears during the day.
That is why you could kill me then, but reviving afterward cost me so much power that now, even at night, I have an appointed death.
―――In other words, I’m no longer immortal, so tell me, Shiki: can you cut the lines on my body?”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Ah---"
"…… If I hadn't been killed by you, I don't think you'd be able to see any at all, but right now you can probably see them.
You see, although I have no 'times of death' during the night, some do appear during the day.
You could kill me because it was during daytime, but you can see my 'time of death' during nighttime now since I've used up a lot of energy to regenerate myself.
---In other words, I've lost my immortality.
So, can you cut the lines on my body, Shiki?"

lines.japanese:
「――――」
　……どうだろう。
　たしかに線があるんだから切れるとは思うけど、あの時のように鮮やかに、一秒もかけずに切断するのは出来そうに無い。
lines.label: s87
lines.maoEnglish:
“……”
I wondered.
There were lines, so I thought I could cut them; but I doubted I could slice her apart as cleanly as I had then, in less than a second.
lines.mao_english:
“……”
I wondered.
There were lines, so I thought I could cut them; but I doubted I could slice her apart as cleanly as I had then, in less than a second.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"-----"
…… Let's see.
I think I probably could, since the lines are there, but I don't think I could do it so briskly and without hesitation like that time before.

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: Looking at Arcueid's faint lines, Shiki says he could not dismember her as cleanly and in under one second as he did before. mirror moon replaces the explicit time limit with 'without hesitation,' changing a judgment about motor performance into a new claim about psychological reluctance.
mirrorMoonErrors.title: Shiki's lost speed and precision become moral hesitation

…… Let's see.
I think I probably could, since the lines are there, but I don't think I could do it so briskly and without hesitation like that time before.

lines.japanese:
「……やりにくいと思う。
線が視えたり視えなかったりするから、アルクェイドが眠ってでもいないかぎり、できない」
「でしょう？
　それが貴方の最大の欠点ね。
どんなに『死』が見えていようとも、その『線』を引くのは志貴自身の腕じゃないといけない。
　いくらわたしが弱ってるからって、志貴に掴まるほど運動能力は低下してないもの」
lines.label: s87
lines.maoEnglish:
“It would be hard. The lines keep fading in and out. I couldn’t do it unless you were asleep or something.”
“Exactly. That is your greatest weakness. However clearly you see ‘death,’ it still takes your own hand to trace the line.
I may be weakened, but not so badly that you could ever catch me.”
lines.mao_english:
“It would be hard. The lines keep fading in and out. I couldn’t do it unless you were asleep or something.”
“Exactly. That is your greatest weakness. However clearly you see ‘death,’ it still takes your own hand to trace the line.
I may be weakened, but not so badly that you could ever catch me.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… I think it'd be hard.
The lines keep fading in and out, so I probably couldn't do it unless you're sleeping."
"You can't, right?
That's your biggest weak point.
No matter how many 'deaths' you can see, you need to trace the line with your own hands.
No matter how weak I am right now, my athletic ability isn't so low that I'd be caught by you."

lines.japanese:
……そっか。
　言われてみれば、俺はすばしっこく動く動物を捕まえることが出来ない。
　捕まえられない、ということは体に触れられないというコト。
　つまり、こんな『線』が見えていても動くモノを殺す事は出来ないってコトか。
lines.label: s87
lines.maoEnglish:
Of course…
I can’t catch a quick-moving animal.
If I can’t catch it, I can’t touch its body.
So even with these lines in sight, I can’t kill anything that can move.
lines.mao_english:
Of course…

So even with these lines in sight, I can’t kill anything that can move.
lines.mirrorMoon:
…… I see.
Come to think of it, I can't catch agile animals.
That means I can't touch their bodies.
In other words, even if I can see its lines, I can't kill anything that moves.
lines.mirror_moon:
…… I see.

lines.japanese:
「―――痛」
　ずきり、と頭痛が走った。
　『線』を見ていると頭痛がおこるのは子供のころから同じだ。
　メガネをかけて視界をもとに戻す。
lines.label: s87
lines.maoEnglish:
“Ow—”
Pain lanced through my head.
Seeing the lines had given me headaches since I was a child.
I put my glasses back on, returning the world to normal.
lines.mao_english:
“Ow—”

I put my glasses back on, returning the world to normal.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"---Ow!"
I feel a stab of pain run through my head.
Looking at the lines gives me a headache, just like it did when I was a child.
I put on my glasses, and the world returns to normal.
lines.mirror_moon:
"---Ow!"

lines.japanese:
「……………」
　アルクェイドはじーっ、とこちらの様子を見つめている。
「……なんだよ。
まだ何かあるのか」
「ううん、そうじゃなくて。
志貴はそのメガネをかけていれば『線』が見えないの？」
「まあ、そうだけど。
昔、俺の目がこうなったときに出会ったひとがくれたんだ。
今じゃレンズだけしか使ってないけど、これのおかげでなんとか普通に生活が送れてるんだよ」
lines.label: s87
lines.maoEnglish:
“……”
Arcueid studied me intently.
“What? Is there still something else?”
“No, that’s not it. Shiki, do those glasses keep you from seeing the lines?”
“More or less. Someone I met when my eyes first became like this gave them to me. I only use the lenses from the original pair now, but thanks to them I can live a reasonably normal life.”
lines.mao_english:
“……”

“No, that’s not it. Shiki, do those glasses keep you from seeing the lines?”
“More or less. Someone I met when my eyes first became like this gave them to me. I only use the lenses from the original pair now, but thanks to them I can live a reasonably normal life.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"………"
Arcueid is staring intently at me.
"…… What?
Is there something else?"
"No, that's not it.
You can't see the lines if you put those glasses on?"
"Yeah.
I got them from someone a long time ago, when my eyes first became like this.
I'm only using the lenses now, but thanks to them, I can lead a normal life."

lines.japanese:
「そっか。
そうだよね、どんなに強いココロがあったって、死とずっと向き合ってたら発狂するか目を潰すしかないものね」
　言いつつ、アルクェイドは近寄ってくる。
lines.label: s87
lines.maoEnglish:
“I see. No matter how strong-willed someone was, if they had to face death without end, they would either go mad or put out their own eyes.”
As she spoke, Arcueid came closer.
lines.mao_english:
“I see. No matter how strong-willed someone was, if they had to face death without end, they would either go mad or put out their own eyes.”
As she spoke, Arcueid came closer.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Yes, I see.
No matter how strong a mind you may have, your only choices when faced with death all the time would be to put out your eyes or go mad."
Saying that, Arcueid comes closer.
lines.mirror_moon:
"Yes, I see.
No matter how strong a mind you may have, your only choices when faced with death all the time would be to put out your eyes or go mad."

lines.japanese:
「ね。
それ、見せて」
「―――ヤだ。
これは大事なものだから、渡さない」
「別に壊したりしないって。
本当に見るだけだからいいでしょ？」
　アルクェイドは力ずくで奪いかねないぐらい、じりじりと近寄ってくる。
　……あやしい。
　自分から『壊したりしない』なんていう所が、すっごく怪しい。
lines.label: s87
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hey. Let me see them.”
“No. They mean too much to me, so I’m not handing them over.”
“I won’t break them. I really only want to look—what’s wrong with that?”
Arcueid inched closer and closer, looking perfectly capable of taking them by force.
Suspicious…
Her volunteering that she ‘wouldn’t break them’ was deeply suspicious.

"Hey.
Can I take a look at them?"
"---No.
These are important to me.
I'm not handing them over to you."
"Come on, I'm not going to break them.
I'm just going to look at them."
Arcueid creeps closer.
I get the feeling she wouldn't be adverse to getting them by force.
…… It's suspicious.
There's something very suspicious about how she says "I'm not going to break them".

lines.japanese:
「―――見るだけでもダメ。
路地裏の時におまえのばか力は思い知らされたからな。
何かのはずみで握り潰されたりしたらどうしようもない」
「むっ。
なによ、そのばか力って。
言っておくけど、通常時の筋力だったら志貴のほうが上なのよ。
わたし、そう無闇に物を壊したりはしないんだから」
　言いつつ、力ずくでメガネを取ろうと手を伸ばしてくるアルクェイド。
　……その態度がますます怪しい。
lines.label: s87
lines.maoEnglish:
“No, you can’t even look. I learned how absurdly strong you are back in that alley. One careless squeeze and you could crush them.”
“Hey! What do you mean, absurdly strong? Under normal circumstances, you’re stronger than I am, Shiki. I don’t just go around breaking things for no reason.”
Even as she said it, Arcueid reached out to wrest the glasses from me.
That only made her more suspicious…

lines.mirrorMoon:
"---Not even just to look at.
I know about your ridiculous powers, after seeing you in that alley.
What would I do if you crushed them by accident?"
"Hey!
What do you mean 'ridiculous powers'?
Let me tell you, in terms of non-fighting strength, you're stronger than I am.
I won't break things at random."
Saying that, Arcueid extends her hands as if she is about to take them by force.
…… Her attitude is becoming more and more suspicious.

とっ、とベッドの上を転がってアルクェイドから離れる。
「あっ、逃げた」
「そりゃあ逃げるよ。
言っとくけどな、このメガネだけは渡さないからな。
万が一にも壊されたりしたら代えがないんだ。
　だいたいな、このメガネがないと正気じゃいられないって言ったのはおまえだろ。
それとも俺にそうなれって言いたいのかよ、おまえは」
lines.label: s87
lines.maoEnglish:
I rolled across the bed, putting distance between us.
“Oh, you ran away!”
“Of course I did. Listen, I’m not giving you these glasses. If you happened to break them, there’s no replacement.
Besides, you’re the one who said I couldn’t stay sane without them. Or are you saying you want me to lose my mind?”

lines.mirrorMoon:
I bounce up off the bed to get away from her.
"Hey, you're running away."
"Of course.
I'll tell you now; I'm not handing over these glasses.
Even if there's only a one in a million chance you'll break them, they're irreplaceable to me.
After all, you're the one who said I wouldn't be able to stay sane without these glasses.
Do you want me to go crazy?"

lines.japanese:
「え―――？
　う、ううん、別にそんなことはないけど」
　……露骨に俺から視線を逸らすアルクェイド。
「―――あのな、アルクェイド。
　何企んでいるかは知らないけど、メガネがなくなったら俺はおまえに協力するどころの話じゃなくなるんだぞ。
四六時中線が見えてたら、気が狂う前に頭痛で頭がパンクしちまうんだから」
lines.label: s87
lines.maoEnglish:
“What—? N-no, of course I don’t.”
Arcueid made an ostentatious show of looking away.
“Arcueid, listen.
I don’t know what you’re plotting, but without these glasses I won’t be in any condition to help you. If I had to see those lines every hour of the day, the headaches would split my skull before I had time to go mad.”
lines.mao_english:
“What—? N-no, of course I don’t.”

“Arcueid, listen.
I don’t know what you’re plotting, but without these glasses I won’t be in any condition to help you. If I had to see those lines every hour of the day, the headaches would split my skull before I had time to go mad.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Huh?
N… no, that's not it at all."
…… Arcueid is obviously trying not to look at me.
"---Come on, Arcueid.
I don't know what you're planning, but if I lose these glasses, I won't be in any position to help you.
If I were to see the lines 24 hours a day, I think I'd die from the headache before I'd go mad."

lines.japanese:
「ふーん。
『死』が視えてると脳に負担がかかるのかしらね。
……うん、志貴の目にはなにかと原因がありそうだけど、とりあえずわたしが教えてあげられるのはこれぐらいかな。
機会があったらもう少し詳しく教えてあげるわ」
「けっこうだよ。
あいにく長話は嫌いでね」
「そうなんだ。
わたしは誰かと話すのって好きだけどな」
　アルクェイドは屈託なく笑った。
　それこそ本当に、ただ話しているだけで楽しいんだよ、というように。
lines.label: s88
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hmm. Perhaps seeing ‘death’ puts a strain on your brain. There seem to be several possible causes behind your eyes, but that’s about all I can tell you for now. If we get the chance, I’ll explain it in more detail.”
“No, thanks. I’ve never cared for long lectures.”
“Really? I like talking to people.”
Arcueid smiled without a care.
As if talking itself was all it took to make her happy.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Hmmm.
I suppose there must be a strain on your brain from being able to see 'death'… Yeah, there's definitely some kind of reason for those eyes of yours, but this is all I can tell you for now.
If we get the chance later, I'll go over it in a little more detail."
"That's alright.
I'm not into long stories anyway."
"Is that so?
Personally, I enjoy talking to other people."
Arcueid gives a carefree laugh.
It really does seem like she enjoys doing nothing more than talking.

lines.japanese:
夜はふけていく。
　アルクェイドはベッドに座り込んでいて、俺も同じようにベッドの上でぼんやりと時計を眺めていた。
　
　時刻は午前四時すぎ。
　夜明けまであと一時間ばかりというところだ。
lines.label: s88
lines.maoEnglish:
The night deepened.
Arcueid sat on the bed, and I sat there too, staring vaguely at the clock.
It was past four in the morning.
Dawn lay only an hour away.

lines.mirrorMoon:
Night descends.
Arcueid sits on the bed and we both stare absentmindedly at the clock.
It's past four in the morning.
About an hour until dawn.

lines.mao_english: A man fled down a corridor. Then a leopard dropped from the ceiling and sheared everything from his nose to the back of his skull away like jelly.
lines.mirrorMoon:

But the panther-like claws descending from the ceiling slice him open from his nose to the back of his head.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
部屋に閉じこもって泣き崩れる女の子。
でも部屋の扉はライオンにしてみれば紙より脆くて、それこそ数秒とかからずにワケノワカラナイ形にされてしまったり。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish: A girl locked herself in her room and collapsed in tears. But to a lion the door was flimsier than paper, and within seconds the girl had been reduced to some incomprehensible shape.
lines.mao_english: A girl locked herself in her room and collapsed in tears. But to a lion the door was flimsier than paper, and within seconds the girl had been reduced to some incomprehensible shape.
lines.mirrorMoon:
A girl locking herself up in a room and crying.
But to the lions, a door is no stronger than paper, and within seconds, they demolish it into an unrecognizable shape.

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: The door is flimsy as paper to the lions; consequently, within seconds the crying girl behind it is reduced to an unrecognizable shape. In mirror moon, the pronoun 'it' attaches the mangling to the door itself, sparing the victim from the action the Japanese explicitly imagines and breaking the sequence's escalating deaths.
mirrorMoonErrors.title: A girl's mutilation is reassigned to the hotel-room door

lines.japanese:
我先にとエレベーターに駆け寄った人たち。
でもエレベーターの中には何十匹という黒犬がつまっていて、エレベーターが開いた瞬間に全員が首をなくしてしまったり。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish: People trampled one another to reach an elevator. But it was packed with dozens of black dogs, and the instant the doors opened, every one of them lost their heads.
lines.mao_english: People trampled one another to reach an elevator. But it was packed with dozens of black dogs, and the instant the doors opened, every one of them lost their heads.
lines.mirrorMoon:
Striving madly to be the first ones there, people dashing for the elevator.
But within it, the black dogs waiting inside decapitate them the instant the doors open.
lines.mirror_moon:
Striving madly to be the first ones there, people dashing for the elevator.
But within it, the black dogs waiting inside decapitate them the instant the doors open.

lines.japanese:
とにかく、誰一人として例外はない。
　この足の下の、ホテルという大きな箱の中。
　そこが、肌で感じ取れるほど身近な地獄絵図だった。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
No one was spared.
Beneath my feet lay the vast interior of the hotel.
Hell was unfolding there, close enough to feel against my skin.
lines.mao_english:
No one was spared.
Beneath my feet lay the vast interior of the hotel.
Hell was unfolding there, close enough to feel against my skin.
lines.mirrorMoon:
At any rate, there is no exception.
Beneath my feet, within this huge box called the hotel…
is a scene from Hell I can feel down to my very bones.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
「ぐ――――」
　吐き気がする。
　だが吐くわけにはいかない。
　そんな事をしていたら―――自分もあの赤い海の一つになると解っている。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
“Ghh—”
Nausea rose in me.
But I couldn’t afford to vomit.
If I stopped for that, I knew I would become another piece of that red sea.
lines.mao_english:
“Ghh—”
Nausea rose in me.
But I couldn’t afford to vomit.
If I stopped for that, I knew I would become another piece of that red sea.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Guuuuh!"
I feel like throwing up.
But I can't do that.
If I just stand around and do that--I'll become a part of that red sea.
lines.mirror_moon:
"Guuuuh!"
I feel like throwing up.

lines.japanese:
「は―――ア。
は。
ア。
は、」
　止まっていた呼吸を再開させる。
　ギリ、と強く歯と歯を噛んだ
　エレベーターの中の犬たちがこちらに気づく。
　気が付けば、下の階からの音は止んでいた。
「…………は」
　つまり。
　もう、生きている者は誰もいないということか。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hah—ah. Hah. Ah. Hah…”
I forced my stalled lungs to breathe again.
I clenched my teeth until they ground together
The dogs in the elevator noticed me.
Only then did I realize that every sound from the floors below had stopped.
“Hah.”
In other words.
There was no one else left alive.

lines.japanese:
グルウウウウウ……
　二匹の黒犬が走りはじめる。
　当然、最後の獲物である俺に向かって。
「は―――――あ」
　黒犬が向かってくる。
　その体には無数の線と、その額には死の点が視えている。
――――だっていうのに。
　麻痺した頭は、戦うことも逃げることも、この体に指示を送ってはくれなかった。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
Grrrrrrrr
The two black dogs broke into a run.
Naturally, they came for me—the last prey remaining.
“Haa―――――ah”
A black dog charged.
Countless lines covered its body, and on its forehead I could see a point of death.
――――And yet.
My numbed mind sent my body no order to fight, and no order to flee.

The black dog is coming for me.
On their bodies, I can see an infinite number of lines, and on their foreheads, the point of death.
----But even so.
My paralyzed mind does not order my body to fight or run.

lines.japanese:
一匹目の黒犬が跳ねる。
　カレらの速さは人間の比ではない。
　十メートル程度の廊下なんて、それこそ二秒とかからなかった。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
The first black dog sprang.
They were incomparably faster than any human.
The first dog covered the ten-meter corridor in less than two seconds.
lines.mao_english:
The first black dog sprang.

The first dog covered the ten-meter corridor in less than two seconds.
lines.mirrorMoon:

Its speed belies all human comparison.

lines.japanese:
黒犬の口が開く。
　俺が持っているナイフなんかより何倍も鋭い牙をノコギリみたいにそろえた口が、的確に喉元へと向かってくる。
　確実かつ迅速。
　カレらが迫ってくる、と認識できた瞬間。
　黒犬の牙は、ガギリ、と音をたてて俺の喉に食いついた。
　遠野志貴は、死んだ。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
Its jaws opened.
Rows of sawlike fangs, many times sharper than my knife, came unerringly for my throat.
Swift.
Certain.
The instant I understood that it had reached me, those fangs closed on my neck with a hard, metallic crunch.
Shiki Tohno died.
lines.mao_english:
Its jaws opened.
Rows of sawlike fangs, many times sharper than my knife, came unerringly for my throat.
Swift.
Certain.
The instant I understood that it had reached me, those fangs closed on my neck with a hard, metallic crunch.
Shiki Tohno died.
lines.mirrorMoon:
They open their mouths.
Mouths filled with fangs so many times sharper than the knife I have, and they are aimed straight at my throat.
Accurate, and fast.
The instant I realize they are drawing upon me,
the fangs bite into my throat with a crunch.
I die.

lines.japanese:
だが、それは間違っている。
　こんなコトぐらいでは殺されないし、死んでもやらない。
　オレは、ヒトが死んでいるぐらいではためらわない。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
But that was wrong.
Something like this could not kill me, and I refused to die.
The mere fact that people were dead was not enough to make me hesitate.
lines.mao_english:
But that was wrong.

The mere fact that people were dead was not enough to make me hesitate.
lines.mirrorMoon:
But that's not right.
I can't be killed by something like this and I refuse to die.
The deaths of others would not cause me to hesitate.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
――――夏の、暑い日。
　ずっと昔、それとも八年も前の昔。
　オレは、もっとひどいコトを、目の当たりにしていたはずじゃないか――――
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
――――A hot summer day.
Long ago—or was eight years ago really so long?
I had witnessed something far worse than this—
lines.mao_english:
――――A hot summer day.
Long ago—or was eight years ago really so long?
I had witnessed something far worse than this—
lines.mirrorMoon:
----A hot summer's day.
It happened long ago, eight years ago.
I've seen something even more terrible----
lines.mirror_moon:
----A hot summer's day.
It happened long ago, eight years ago.
I've seen something even more terrible----

lines.japanese:
ざく。
　首筋に噛みついた黒犬の額に、ナイフを突きたてた。
　黒犬が俺の首に噛みついて、そのまま噛み切ろうとするよりわずかだけ先に、腕が動いてくれたのだ。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
The blade struck home.
I drove the knife into the forehead of the black dog clamped around my neck.
My arm moved a fraction of a second before its jaws could bite through.
lines.mao_english:
The blade struck home.
I drove the knife into the forehead of the black dog clamped around my neck.
My arm moved a fraction of a second before its jaws could bite through.
lines.mirrorMoon:
Thrust.
I thrust my knife into the forehead of the black dog biting into my neck.
My arm moved just before the black dog ripped through my throat.
lines.mirror_moon:
Thrust.
I thrust my knife into the forehead of the black dog biting into my neck.
My arm moved just before the black dog ripped through my throat.

lines.japanese:
自分でもほれぼれする。
　まるでモノを斬る機能しかない機械みたいに、無駄なく目の前にある犬の眉間にナイフを刺した。
　そこが一匹目の犬の『点』だったからだ。
　普通、脳が破損しても筋肉というものは脳の下した命令を実行しようとする。
　頭を貫いたところで、黒犬の口は俺の首を噛みきるだろう。
　ああ、まあ―――その、普通なら。
　だが、黒犬は『死』んでいる。
　死は停止だ。
こいつは俺に殺された時点で、あらゆる効力を失った。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
It was beautiful, even to me.
With the perfect economy of a machine made only to cut, I planted the knife between the dog’s eyes.
That was the first dog’s point.
Ordinarily, even after the brain is destroyed, muscles continue trying to carry out its final commands.
Merely piercing its skull would not stop its jaws from tearing through my throat.
Yes, ordinarily.
But the black dog was dead.
Death meant cessation. From the instant I killed it, everything in it stopped.

lines.mirrorMoon:
It was done so perfectly, even for myself.
Like a machine whose sole function is to cut, I plunged the knife into the dog's forehead without any useless and wasted movement.
Because that is where the first dog's "point" was.
Normally, even if the brain is destroyed, the muscles try to execute the commands they have received from the brain.
The black dog would have probably ripped through my throat even if I had simply pierced its head.
Well--normally, that would happen.
But the black dog is "dead".
Death is a complete stoppage.
At the point when I killed it, it lost every form of validity.

　が、それは間違いだった。
　コイツの『点』は顔ではなく胸にある。
　口を刺したところで、すぐに死んでなどはくれない。

The first dog dropped to the floor.
In its place, the other sprang straight at my face.
“……”
I thrust the knife into its open mouth.
A mistake.
This one’s point wasn’t in its face, but its chest.
A blade through the mouth would not kill it quickly.

lines.japanese:
ナイフは黒犬の口内から後頭部まで通過した。
　自然、ナイフを持った手は黒犬の口の中に納まってしまう。
「――――――あ」
　黒犬はまだ生きている。
　アゴがしめられる。
　ナイフを持った手と腕の間、軟骨という柔らかいジョイント部分が、そのまま噛み千切られようとする。
　その痛みで、ようやく、まともな思考が戻ってくれた。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
The knife passed from inside its mouth through the back of its skull.
Naturally, the hand gripping it ended up inside the dog’s jaws.
“—Ah.”
The black dog was still alive.
Its jaws closed.
They bore down on the soft cartilage of my wrist, ready to bite straight through.
That pain finally restored my ability to think.

　だん、と床に倒れこむ。
　それでも腕は抜けない。

「っっっっっっっっ！」

I slammed onto the floor.
My arm remained trapped.
Though the knife transfixed it, the dog only clenched harder.
“Nngh…!”
My arm—it was going to tear my arm off!
Impossible; no dog should still be able to bite in this state…!

lines.japanese:
「っ、こ、こいつ……！」
　ぬらりとした感触。
　見れば黒犬の口から、ボタボタと血がこぼれだしている。
　頭をナイフで貫かれた黒犬の血か。
　それとも、食いちぎられようとしている俺の腕から流れている血か。
―――正直、そんなコト。
　　　痛みなんかより頭が混乱していて、
　　　どうでもいい問題だった。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
“Y-you…!”
Something slick ran over me.
Blood dripped steadily from the dog’s mouth.
Was it the dog’s, from the knife through its skull?
Or mine, from the arm it was trying to sever?
―――Honestly, I didn’t care.
My head was too confused even to register the pain—
It simply didn’t matter whose blood it was.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… Y-you…!"
I feel something wet.
I can see blood spilling from the black dog's mouth.
Is it the black dog's blood, leaking from its knife wound to the head?
Or is the blood coming from my arm, about to be torn off?
---To be honest…
My head is too messed up to be feeling the pain,
so it isn't a big deal which one it is.

The way to survive was brutally simple.

　ついでに言うと、ナイフを握った遠野志貴の腕も、もう完全に頭を突き破って出てきている。

evidence.mirrorMoon:
Without a sound, the blade of the knife punctures out the back of the black dog's head.
It's as if the dog has grown a horn.
Having split the skull, I easily slash through its skin.
Blood and brains spray out as the knife completely emerges from the back of the head.
Also, the hand gripping the knife travels completely through.

　血だらけの指からナイフを引き剥がして、自由になっている腕でナイフを持ちなおす。
　そのまま、黒犬の胸の『点』を貫いた。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hah…
haaah…”
The dog was still alive.
Then only one task remained.
I reached over with my other arm, pried the knife from my blood-slick fingers, and took it in my free hand.
Then I pierced the point in the dog’s chest.

lines.japanese:
「は――――あ」
　黒犬はそれで死んだ。
　アゴにかかっていた力もなくなって、腕はあっけなく引きぬけた。
「なんだ―――全然食い込んでないじゃないか」
　血だらけの腕を見る。
　たしかに牙の形に傷はあるけれど、肉はまったくといっていいほど無傷だ。
　この血は頭を貫かれた黒犬のものだろう。
　噛まれている時の痛みなんて些細なもので、こちらの恐怖が痛みを何倍にも感じさせていただけだ。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
“Haaah…”
That killed it.
The strength left its jaws, and my arm slipped free with ridiculous ease.
“It barely broke the skin.”
I examined my blood-soaked arm.
The fangs had certainly left their marks, but the flesh itself was almost entirely unharmed.
The blood must have belonged to the dog whose skull I had pierced.
The bite had barely hurt; my terror had magnified the pain many times over.

lines.mirrorMoon:
*gasp* *pant*
And with that, the black dog dies.
The strength drains from its jaws, and I easily pull my arm back out.
"Oh--it wasn't torn off at all."
I look at my blood-covered arm.
There are many teeth marks, but the flesh is almost free of wounds.
The blood must have been from the black dog when I impaled it through the head.
The pain from when I was being bitten was really quite trivial, but my fear must have amplified it many times over.

lines.label: s90

“Haaah…”
Still lying on the floor, I stared at the ceiling.
My head hurt.
The world had become a patchwork of seams, with black points of death visible everywhere.
My whole body was frozen, while reason alone burned in a delirious fever.

lines.japanese:
「―――く」
　すぐ近くには二匹の黒犬の死体。
　片腕は血にまみれていて、もう片腕には赤いナイフ。
　……ついでに言うのなら、床の下の階層には数え切れないほどの人の死体。
「――――は、はは、ははは」
　笑うしかない。
　だって、こんなのは現実じゃない。
　こんなのが現実であるはずがない。
　俺はいつから、瞳をあけたままで、悪い夢なんかを観てしまっているんだろう―――？
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
“Kh.”
Two black dogs lay dead beside me.
One arm was drenched in blood; the other held a red knife.
And, incidentally, the floors beneath this one contained more human corpses than I could count.
“Hahahahaha.”
There was nothing to do but laugh.
This wasn’t reality.
Nothing like this could possibly be real.
How long had I been dreaming this nightmare with my eyes wide open?

キンコーン。
「え――――？」
　ひどく場違いな明るい音がした。
「くそ、なんだこの頭痛―――」
　刃物で突き刺されるような頭痛を堪えながら立ちあがる。
「エレ……ベーター……？」
　今のはもう一つのエレベーターが上がってきた音らしい。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
Ding.
“Huh—?”
A bright, cheerful chime rang out, grotesquely out of place.
“Damn it, what is this headache—”
Enduring a pain like a blade through my skull, I struggled upright.
“The elevator?”
Apparently the other elevator had arrived.

lines.mirrorMoon:

"Eh--?"
A terribly out-of-place cheerful sound rings out.
"Damn it, what's with this headache--?"
I stand up, enduring the razor-like pain in my head.
"Ele… vator…?"
It seems the sound is the other elevator coming up.

lines.japanese:
扉が開く。
　その中には、黒いコートを着た男が一人。
　頭痛が、一段と強くなる。
「あいつ――――」
　そう、見たことがある。
　たしかに、自分はあの男を見たコトがあったはずだ。
「―――――――」
　男は無言で向かってくる。
「おまえ―――！」
　ナイフを構えて男を睨んだ。
「―――――――」
　けれど、男はまったく反応しないで歩いてくる。
　こちらのことなど、まるっきり眼中にないというふうに。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
The doors opened.
Inside stood a single man in a black coat.
The pain in my head intensified.
“That man—”
Yes.
I was certain I had seen him before.
“……”
The man approached in silence.
“You—!”
I raised my knife and glared.
“……”
But the man kept coming without the slightest reaction.
He walked as if I did not even exist.

"-------"

　その、血走った目。
　人間の持つ目とは逸脱したその目を見た瞬間、俺の体の自由は、まるっきりきかなくなった。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
The distance narrowed.
He came within a single meter before he finally seemed to notice me.
Those bloodshot eyes.
The instant I saw eyes so far removed from anything human, every part of my body ceased to obey me.

lines.mirrorMoon:

Just a little more---when there is barely one meter between us, and the man finally seems to notice me.
Those bloodshot eyes.
The instant I see those eyes which no human should possess, I lose all freedom to move my body.

　男はぐるり、と廊下に転がる二匹の黒犬の死体を見た。
「――塵どもめ。
肉片ひとつ片づけられぬのでは、我が肉体である資格はない」

―――壊れてる。
　黒い犬たちは、びゅるん、と音をたてて、液体になって男のコートの中に消えてしまった。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
“I thought I had slaughtered them all, but one remains.”
The man swept his gaze over the two black dogs sprawled in the corridor.
“Wretched refuse. If you cannot dispose of a single scrap of meat, you are unfit to be my flesh.”
He muttered in distaste and raised one arm.
His coat lifted like a great black cape.
―――Broken.
With a liquid rush, the black dogs dissolved and vanished beneath the man’s coat.

　叫び声さえ、あげられない。
　男のコートの下は真っ黒で、輪郭というものしか存在しなかった。
　そこにあるのは、ただ、泥のような闇だった。
「やば―――――――」
　やばい。

　そう本能が危険信号をかき鳴らしているっていうのに、指先一つまともには動いてくれない。

lines.maoEnglish:
“Ah—”
I couldn’t even scream.
Beneath his coat was pure black, nothing but an outline.
Nothing lay there but darkness as thick as mud.
“This is bad—”
Bad.
This thing was far too dangerous—
Every instinct shrieked its warning, yet I couldn’t properly move so much as a fingertip.

「――――――！」

―――――But it was already too late.
The man stood before me.
His eyes were not on me at all.

　スラリ、とコートの片腕があがる。
　その下の混沌とした闇。
　そこから、何か巨大なモノが現れた。
　ごう、と。
　二つの風切り音が閉じられる。
　男のコートの下から現れたソレは、人間を軽く丸呑みできそうなワニの口だった。

lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
“Devour.”
One arm of the coat rose with elegant ease.
Beneath it lay churning, chaotic darkness.
Something enormous emerged from within.
With a roar.
Two currents of rushing air snapped shut.
What had emerged beneath the man’s coat was the maw of a crocodile large enough to swallow a human whole.
“Ah—”
I was going to die.
Crumpled in an instant like a sheet of wastepaper.
The moment certainty struck, someone’s hand wrenched me backward.

"Feed."
He raises one of his arms.
Below it lies a chaotic darkness.
From there, something huge appears.
Whomp.
The sound of wind.
That which has appeared from below the man's coat is a crocodile's mouth, easily large enough to swallow a man whole.
"Ah------"
I'm going to die.
Right here, in an instant, crunched up like a ball of paper.
Just as I was convinced of this, someone pulls me back.

lines.japanese:
ぞぶり、という音。
「なっ―――」
　信じ、られない。
　ワニのアギトは俺ではなく、俺の体をひっぱってくれたアルクェイドの腹に食らいついた。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
A wet crunch.
“Wha—”
Impossible.
The crocodile’s jaws had closed not on me, but around the abdomen of Arcueid—the one who had dragged me away.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
Clomp.
"Wha--!?"
I… can't believe it.
Instead of me, the jaws of the crocodile clamp onto the stomach of Arcueid, who just pulled me out of the way.

lines.japanese:
「つ――――！」
　アルクェイドの顔が苦痛に歪む。
　彼女はワニの口に完全に食いつかれる前に後ろに引き下がった。
「…………」
　男は無言でアルクェイドを凝視する。
　アルクェイドは腹を真っ赤に染めたまま、苦しげに男を睨み返していた。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
“Tch—!”
Arcueid’s face twisted in pain.
Before the jaws could fasten completely, she pulled back.
“……”
The man stared at Arcueid in silence.
Her stomach stained scarlet, she returned his gaze through the pain.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Ssstt--!"
Arcueid's face contorts in agony.
She draws back before she is completely devoured by the crocodile's maw.
"…………"
The man silently watches Arcueid.
Arcueid glares back at him with a pained expression, her mid-section stained in red.

lines.japanese:
「―――信じられない。
混沌とも名づけられた吸血種が、こんなくだらないゲームにのってくるなんて。
なんだか出来の悪い夢みたいだわ、ネロ・カオス」
「同感だな。
私も、真祖の生き残りを捕らえるなど、そのような無謀な祭りの執行者にしたてあげられるとは夢にも思わなかった。
私にとっても、これは悪夢だ」
　ネロ、とか呼ばれた男は静かに腕をさげる。
　コートはもとに戻って、ワニの口もその下に消えてしまった。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
“—Unbelievable. That a member of the vampiric species known as Chaos would stoop to playing such a pathetic game. This feels like a particularly bad dream, Nrvnqsr Chaos.”
“On that, we agree. Never did I imagine I would be made the officiant of so reckless a festival—the capture of a surviving True Ancestor. This is a nightmare for me as well.”
The man she had called Nrvnqsr lowered his arm.
His coat settled into place, and the crocodile’s maw vanished beneath it.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"---I can't believe a vampire named Chaos would play such trivial games.
It's like a poorly-scripted nightmare, Nrvnqsr Chaos."
"I feel the same way.
To catch one of the surviving True Ancestors… I never dreamed I would be a part of such a foolish festival.
This is a nightmare for me, too."
The man called Nrvnqsr quietly lowers his arm.
The coat returns to its former position, and the crocodile's mouth disappears underneath.

lines.japanese:
男はアルクェイドだけを視界に収めている。
　彼女に守られて、その後ろでナイフを構えている俺のことなんてまったく見えていないみたいに。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
The man’s vision held only Arcueid.
Sheltered behind her with my knife raised, I might as well have been invisible.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
The man looks only at Arcueid.
It's as if he's not concerned at all about me, standing behind her with my knife raised.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
「しかし、これはどういう事だ？
　私の前の執行者は貴様に傷一つ付けられなかったという話だが、それはどのような間違いなのだ。
　今の貴様の存在規模は脆弱すぎる。
一介の亡者にも劣るその衰退―――私が来る前に教会の者たちに襲われたか、アルクェイド・ブリュンスタッド」
「………………」
　アルクェイドは何も言わない。
　男は、感情のない目でアルクェイドを凝視する。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
“Yet what is this? I was told my predecessor could not put so much as a scratch upon you; how am I to reconcile that claim with what I see?
The scale of your existence has withered beyond belief. You have fallen beneath even a common corpse—were you attacked by agents of the Church before my arrival, Arcueid Brunestud?”
“……”
Arcueid said nothing.
The man watched her with emotionless eyes.
lines.mao_english:
“Yet what is this? I was told my predecessor could not put so much as a scratch upon you; how am I to reconcile that claim with what I see?
The scale of your existence has withered beyond belief. You have fallen beneath even a common corpse—were you attacked by agents of the Church before my arrival, Arcueid Brunestud?”
“……”
Arcueid said nothing.
The man watched her with emotionless eyes.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"But what is going on?
I have heard that the previous executor could not even scratch you.
What kind of a mistake is this?
Right now, your presence is exceedingly weak.
Even weaker than a mere member of The Dead--were you attacked by The Church before I arrived, Arcueid Brunestud?"
"……………"
Arcueid says nothing.
The man fixes his emotionless stare on her.

lines.japanese:
「……解せぬな。
貴様を害せるほどの概念武装は限られている。
アレを保有しているのは教会の殺し屋どもだけだ。
このような極東の地に、埋葬機関が派遣されるとは思えぬが」
　男はかすかに瞳を細めると、くるりと背を向けた。
「だが、どちらにせよ私にとっては僥倖だ。
貴様がそこまで弱っている是非は問わぬ。
勝機があるうちに、その首を貰い受けるのみだ」
「っ……！」
　ナイフを構えて男の攻撃に備える。
lines.label: s90
lines.maoEnglish:
“…I do not understand. Few conceptual weapons can injure you to this degree, and only the Holy Church’s assassins possess that particular one. I cannot imagine the Burial Agency being dispatched to this remote corner of the Far East.”
His eyes narrowed almost imperceptibly, and he turned away.
“In any event, your condition is a stroke of fortune for me. How or why you became so weak is irrelevant. While victory lies within my reach, I need only claim your head.”
“Tch…!”
I raised my knife, bracing for his attack.
